<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/control/codex/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.

{
  "ambiguities": [
    "The perturbations are arbitrary real labels at internal nodes. No floating-point format, rounding rule, probabilistic model, or realizability condition is specified.",
    "The target proof is excluded from the dossier. The translation describes the supplied proposition and definitions, without auditing its proof."
  ],
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "effect_on_target": "This is the sole explicit hypothesis: every internal-node perturbation has absolute value at most the same real u.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For every n ∈ ℕ, t ∈ T_n, e ∈ E(t), and u ∈ ℝ, define B(e,u) recursively by B(leafError,u) = True and B(nodeError(eL,eR,δ),u) = B(eL,u) ∧ (B(eR,u) ∧ |δ| ≤ u).",
      "name": "Uniform perturbation bound",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The variable errors specifies one real perturbation at each internal node of the given tree.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "E(t), for n ∈ ℕ and t ∈ T_n, is an inductive type of decorations of t. Its constructors are leafError ∈ E(leaf) and nodeError(eL,eR,δ) ∈ E(node(l,r)) for eL ∈ E(l), eR ∈ E(r), and δ ∈ ℝ.",
      "name": "Tree-indexed perturbation decorations",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "This is the perturbed evaluation on the left side of the asserted identity.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "For n ∈ ℕ, t ∈ T_n, e ∈ E(t), and v : Fin n → ℝ, define R(e,v) recursively. At a leaf, R(leafError,v) = v(0). For l ∈ T_m, r ∈ T_k, and e = nodeError(eL,eR,δ), set R(e,v) = (R(eL,vL) + R(eR,vR))(1+δ), where vL(i)=v(i) for i<m and vR(j)=v(m+j) for j<k.",
      "name": "Multiplicatively perturbed tree summation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The right side sums this list with initial ancestor factor 1. Each internal node contributes its exact subtree sum times its own perturbation and all strict-ancestor factors.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For A ∈ ℝ, n ∈ ℕ, t ∈ T_n, e ∈ E(t), and v : Fin n → ℝ, define the real list C(A,e,v). At a leaf it is empty. At e = nodeError(eL,eR,δ), with underlying t = node(l,r), it is (C(A(1+δ),eL,vL) ++ C(A(1+δ),eR,vR)) ++ [(A S(t,v))δ]. Thus entries occur in left-subtree, right-subtree, current-node order.",
      "name": "Ancestor-weighted error contribution list",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The target ranges over finite ordered full binary summation trees indexed by their number of leaves.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "T_n, indexed by n ∈ ℕ, is the inductively generated family with leaf ∈ T_1 and node(l,r) ∈ T_(m+k) for l ∈ T_m and r ∈ T_k. There is no empty-tree constructor.",
      "name": "Leaf-count-indexed binary trees",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "This supplies the exact reference value subtracted from R and the exact subtree sums used in C.",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For n ∈ ℕ, t ∈ T_n, and v : Fin n → ℝ, define S(t,v) recursively by S(leaf,v)=v(0) and S(node(l,r),v)=S(l,vL)+S(r,vR). This is the exact real sum of the n leaf entries in their tree order.",
      "name": "Exact tree summation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Implements the leaf and node cases in the definition of B without adding a hypothesis.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "For any universe level q and family M(n,t,e,u) : Sort q, given n, t ∈ T_n, e ∈ E(t), u ∈ ℝ, a value of M(1,leaf,leafError,a) for every a ∈ ℝ, and a value of M(m+k,node(l,r),nodeError(eL,eR,δ),a) for every m,k,l,r,eL,eR,δ,a of the corresponding types, this dependent case splitter returns M(n,t,e,u). It uses equality transports to align indices and provides no recursive hypotheses.",
      "name": "Decoration case analysis with a real parameter",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Packages recursive results for B, R, and C; the child results accessed in their definitions are the first components of the respective child packages.",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "For any family M(n,t,e) : Sort q, define a descendant-result type D_M(e) : Sort(max(1,q)). At leafError it is the singleton type PUnit. At nodeError(eL,eR,δ) it is (M(m,l,eL) × D_M(eL)) × (M(k,r,eR) × D_M(eR)), using universe-polymorphic products.",
      "name": "Decoration descendant-result packages",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the structural recursive mechanism defining B, R, and C.",
      "id": "D009",
      "meaning": "For any M(n,t,e) : Sort q, any n,t,e, and a step F which for every n,t,e maps D_M(e) to M(n,t,e), return the recursively constructed value of M(n,t,e). The body takes the first component of the value-and-descendants pair constructed by D020.",
      "name": "Course-of-values recursion on decorations",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Leaves have no perturbation parameter, are evaluated exactly, satisfy B for every u, and contribute no list entries.",
      "id": "D010",
      "meaning": "leafError is the constructor of E(leaf), where leaf has exactly one leaf.",
      "name": "Leaf decoration",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Introduces the local δ responsible for the factor 1+δ and the current-node contribution.",
      "id": "D011",
      "meaning": "For all m,k ∈ ℕ, l ∈ T_m, r ∈ T_k, eL ∈ E(l), eR ∈ E(r), and δ ∈ ℝ, nodeError(eL,eR,δ) belongs to E(node(l,r)). The constructor itself places no bound on δ.",
      "name": "Perturbed internal-node constructor",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Allows the numeral 0 to be interpreted as an element of Fin 1 in the leaf case of R.",
      "id": "D012",
      "meaning": "The natural number 0+1 is nonzero.",
      "name": "Nonzero singleton index size",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Implements the leaf and node cases of R and C while preserving the vector's dimension.",
      "id": "D013",
      "meaning": "For any M(n,t,e,v) : Sort q, given n,t,e,v, a leaf value M(1,leaf,leafError,w) for every w : Fin 1 → ℝ, and a node value M(m+k,node(l,r),nodeError(eL,eR,δ),w) for every m,k,l,r,eL,eR,δ and w : Fin(m+k) → ℝ, return M(n,t,e,v). It is dependent case analysis with equality transports and no recursive hypotheses.",
      "name": "Decoration case analysis with a leaf vector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Packages the child evaluations used by the recursive definition of S.",
      "id": "D014",
      "meaning": "For any family M(n,t) : Sort q, define H_M(t) : Sort(max(1,q)). At leaf it is PUnit; at node(l,r), with l ∈ T_m and r ∈ T_k, it is (M(m,l) × H_M(l)) × (M(k,r) × H_M(r)).",
      "name": "Tree descendant-result packages",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the recursive mechanism defining exact summation S.",
      "id": "D015",
      "meaning": "For any M(n,t) : Sort q, any n ∈ ℕ and t ∈ T_n, and a step F assigning M(a,s) to every a ∈ ℕ, s ∈ T_a, and package H_M(s), construct M(n,t) recursively. The result is the first component of D023.",
      "name": "Course-of-values recursion on trees",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Justifies explicitly constructing the index 0 ∈ Fin 1 in S's leaf case.",
      "id": "D016",
      "meaning": "In the natural-number order, 0 < 1.",
      "name": "Validity of the singleton leaf index",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
